clients.name: Quarter Athletic
clients.summary: Centralize Quarter Athletic's operational workflow so leadership can see what is happening, who is responsible, what happens next, and what is stuck.

facts.currentProcess: Pen, paper, leadership memory, verbal communication and disconnected files

clients.objective: Define and build an MVP that centralizes the workflow from customer/project intake through design, financial processing, production, quality assurance, packaging and shipping.
nextActions: Walk through one real completed Quarter Athletic order end-to-end
Confirm the actual production stages and handoffs
Confirm employee departments, roles and access needs
Document the current quoting, invoicing and payment process
Confirm MVP scope before production development begins

originalMeeting.title: Initial Discovery Meeting
transcription: Leadership needs visibility into everything being done.
Project: mockups; customer chooses what they like / what is good to go.
There is always a point of contact.
Production: manager, approximately 52 people, quality assurance and producing.
Shipping: processing and putting products in nice bags.
Right-side notes reference three divisions and additional ideas that still need confirmation.
confirmedStatements: The president and vice president currently carry a large amount of operational knowledge themselves.
Pen and paper are still part of the current management process.
A clear point of contact is important in the workflow.
The operation includes design/mockups, quotes/invoices, production, QA, packaging and shipping.
originalMeeting.interpretation: The core need is not simply task management. Quarter Athletic needs an internal operating system that converts leadership memory and paper-based coordination into visible, trackable company knowledge.
uncertainNotes: Exact meaning of the handwritten '3 divisions' note.
A possible recruiting-platform reference on the right side of the page.
Any external website or division name written in the lower-right area.

Customer process: How does a new team/customer enter Quarter Athletic?
Who normally handles the first meeting?
When does an opportunity officially become a project/order?
Products: How are products, sizes, colors and options represented today?
Can one project contain several product types and size breakdowns?
Mockups: Who creates mockups and where are source files stored?
How are mockups sent to customers and how is approval captured?
How many revisions are typical and what happens after approval?
Quotes and invoices: Who creates quotes and how is pricing calculated?
Are deposits required or is full payment required before production?
What software currently creates invoices and records payments?
Production: What are the actual production stages from approved order to finished product?
How is work assigned across the production staff?
Do different product types follow different production workflows?
Quality assurance: What exactly constitutes a QA pass?
Does every item get inspected or is sampling used?
What happens to failed items and who approves rework?
Shipping: Which carriers are used and how are labels generated?
Can a project ship in multiple packages or partial shipments?
How is delivery confirmation handled today?
Employees and access: Which employees actually need platform access?
What information should each role be allowed to see or change?

meetings.title: Initial Discovery Meeting
meetings.summary: Initial discussion of the management problem, current paper/memory workflow and the desire for a centralized company tracker.
meetings.decisions: Proceed with deeper discovery before finalizing the build scope and pricing.
meetings.followUp: Run a detailed workflow session with leadership using one real order as the example.

requirements.title: Project ownership
requirements.description: Every active project must have a clearly identified Quarter Athletic owner and a customer/team point of contact.

requirements.title: Leadership visibility
requirements.description: Leadership must be able to see active work, ownership, current stage, deadlines and blockers without relying on memory.

requirements.title: Mockup version tracking
requirements.description: The system should maintain mockup/design versions and indicate customer feedback and the final approved version.

requirements.title: Operational finance tracking
requirements.description: Projects should connect to quotes, invoices, balances and payment status without attempting to replace full accounting in the MVP.

requirements.title: Production queue
requirements.description: Approved work should enter a visible production queue with responsibility, priority, quantity, due date and status.

requirements.title: QA gate before shipping
requirements.description: Production work should record QA pass/fail and required rework before an order is allowed to move to shipping.

requirements.title: Activity history
requirements.description: Significant project changes should create a permanent activity trail so company knowledge no longer lives only in individual memory.

mvp.target: Preliminary MVP target: approximately 8–12 weeks, subject to workflow validation.
